title: Developer Experience Canonical Patchbook and API Examples
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical Developer Experience (DevX) patchbook: a combined quick-reference of SDK initialization patterns, reproducible API examples, top support issues with deterministic fixes, and the docs-site operating checklist used by the DevX team when publishing or triaging docs changes. It is intended for engineers and developer-facing support reps handling SDK, example, or docs-site problems.

Scope

- SDK quickstarts and minimal integration templates (Python, Node, Go).
- API examples used in docs & sample apps (auth, streaming, function/tool calling).
- Canonical trouble-ticket triage and fixes for the top issues we see in support.
- Docs site CI/publishing and rollback procedures.

Audience

- Developer Experience engineers
- SDK maintainers
- Support engineers and Solutions Engineers
- Docs authors and DevRel

Owner and Escalation

- Primary owner: DevX (eng-developer-experience)
- Secondary: Runtime SDK owners (see SDK OWNER doc for team mapping)
- Escalation path: Support -> DevX triage -> SDK owner -> Runtime oncall

Priority SLOs

- Initial triage on incoming DevX support ticket: 4 hours (P1/P2: 1 hour).
- Confirmed reproducible bug or docs regression: acknowledge within 24 hours.
- Target resolution or a mitigation rollout (canary) within 72 hours for P2; 24 hours for P1.

Canonical Quickstarts (minimum working examples)

NOTE: All examples assume REDWOOD_API_KEY is set in the environment and that the customer is using the hosted Redwood API. Replace region/model names with customer-specific values when appropriate.

1) Python (requests, streaming friendly)

Code (python):

```python
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
BASE = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1"

def simple_generate(prompt: str):
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    payload = {"model": "redwood-optimized-1", "input": prompt, "max_tokens": 128}
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/generate", json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print(simple_generate("Summarize the following: ..."))
```

Notes: use requests timeout to avoid silent hangs. For streaming, use the /stream endpoint with chunked decoding.

2) Node (fetch + streaming example)

Code (node):

```javascript
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;

async function gen(prompt) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-optimized-1', input: prompt })
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}

module.exports = { gen }
```

3) Go (minimal HTTP)

Code (go):

```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "encoding/json"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  payload := map[string]interface{}{
    "model":"redwood-optimized-1",
    "input":"Explain mutexes simply"
  }
  b, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(b))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  var out map[string]interface{}
  json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out)
  fmt.Printf("%v\n", out)
}
```

Error handling patterns (recommended)

- Always check for HTTP 401/403: treat as invalid API key or scope mismatch.
- 429: surface quota/rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) to caller.
- 5xx: retry with exponential backoff (jitter) up to 3 attempts for idempotent requests.
- Streaming connections: implement keepalive and reconnect heuristics on transient network errors.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes

Table: Issue | Symptom | Typical Root Cause | Canonical Fix | Notes

- Authentication failures
  - Symptom: 401 / "invalid_api_key" returned immediately.
  - Root cause: API key rotated, or team used a key for a different environment.
  - Fix: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY in environment, verify key via `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status`. If key expired, issue a new key via Console -> API Keys and update CI secret.

- Rate-limited requests (429)
  - Symptom: Bursts of 429s during load testing; X-RateLimit headers present.
  - Root cause: Client does not implement batching or global concurrency limits.
  - Fix: Implement client-side concurrency cap (e.g., token-bucket) and enable request-level batching. Suggest Redwood Optimize recommendations: batch_size=16 for short prompts, 8 for long sequences. Check quota in Console.

- Latency spikes for generation
  - Symptom: sudden increase in p95 latency, timeouts in client.
  - Root cause: Mismatched model variant (heavy quantization), cold KV-cache, or routing to remote region.
  - Fix: Verify model variant and region in request; for latency-sensitive paths pin to a low-latency model variant or Dedicated pool. Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. See Performance Standards doc for SLO selection.

- Garbled or truncated output (reproducible)
  - Symptom: tokens cut mid-word or repeated tails.
  - Root cause: improper streaming handling or premature connection close by a reverse proxy (e.g., nginx default timeouts).
  - Fix: Ensure proxies have increased read/write timeouts (recommend >= 120s for long streams), use chunked transfer encoding, and validate client collects all chunks until stream end.

- Embedding drift / bogus similarity results
  - Symptom: search returns semantically irrelevant results after a model update.
  - Root cause: model upgrade without re-embedding corpus or index mismatch.
  - Fix: Recompute embeddings using the new model variant and rebuild indexes. Use Redwood Optimize to recommend an embedding quantization profile.

- SDK upgrade regressions
  - Symptom: previously working examples fail after SDK minor bump.
  - Root cause: breaking change introduced without migration guide.
  - Fix: Revert to pinned SDK version and open SDK PR documenting the breaking change; write migration snippet and add to SDK upgrade guide.

Repro & Triage Playbook (numbered steps)

1. Reproduce locally using the minimal quickstart for the language specified by the reporter.
2. Capture a failing log set with timing: request payload (redact PII), headers (redact auth values), and full HTTP trace.
3. Run the same request against the API status endpoint to confirm service health.
4. If 5xx or 429, collect request IDs and escalate to runtime oncall with reproducible snippet and load profile.
4a. For auth/403: confirm project/org scoping in Console.
5. If output quality regression, run prompt against pinned previous model variant to determine regression window.
6. Document fix and add a canonical snippet to this page if it will be reused.

Docs-site Operating Procedure (publishing checklist)

- Local authoring: run `make docs-serve` to preview site.
- Pre-PR checks: run `make docs-lint` and `make docs-spellcheck`.
- Generate API example snapshots: `make examples-snapshot` — this runs quickstarts in a hermetic container and captures payloads.
- CI checks: linter, link-checker, accessibility check, and examples snapshot verification.
- Review: assign at least one reviewer from DevX and one SDK owner.
- Merge: merge to main branch; CI will build and deploy to staging automatically.
- Staging smoke: run `scripts/staging-smoke.sh` to confirm sample pages load and examples run.
- Publish: trigger release pipeline via the Docs Console (button in the pipeline). Add release notes and cherrypick tag if backport required.

Rollback procedure

1. If post-publish defects are detected, open a rollback PR reverting the commit(s) on the docs site repo.
2. Mark the PR title with `[ROLLBACK][HOTFIX]` and assign DevX lead for expedited review.
3. When merged, CI will deploy the previous build. Confirm via staging smoke and inform affected customers.

Canonical Reply Templates (support -> customer)

- Initial acknowledgement (use in ticket):

"Thanks for the report — we’ve received your ticket and will triage within 4 hours. To help us reproduce, please attach: the failing minimal code snippet, HTTP headers (with Authorization redacted), request timestamp (UTC), and any Retry-After/X-Request-Id headers you observed."

- After root cause identified (example):

"Root cause: your app exceeded the configured concurrency cap in the SDK which triggered downstream 429s during burst load. Recommended mitigation: upgrade to SDK vX.Y.Z (contains token-bucket limiter), add client-side retry with exponential backoff, or request increased throughput via Console -> Quotas. We can help schedule a short pairing session to update your client."

Maintenance and Long-term Improvements

- Quarterly: refresh code samples across languages and run examples-snapshot to ensure they execute.
- Post-release: add any recurring support patterns as new rows in this document.
- Add automated fuzz tests that run quickstarts against staging every commit to catch regressions early.

Appendix: Issue Report Template (paste into new support ticket)

- Title: [LANG] Short description (e.g., Python: 429 bursts during bulk index)
- Steps to reproduce: (1) minimal snippet (2) exact request payload (3) environment and SDK version
- Observed: HTTP status, headers, body snippets
- Expected: what the customer expected to see
- Impact: severity, number of users, and whether production blocking
- Attachments: logs, request ids, example timestamps

If you add a new canonical fix to this page, add yourself as a reviewer and ping #devx on Slack so we can vet the change and update the examples-snapshot job.
